content.text:
I replaced the always-visible table BubbleMenu in `frontend/src/scenes/notebooks/Notebook/TableMenu.tsx` with the grip handles from your draft. `Editor.tsx` still renders `<TableMenu />`, so no other files changed. I haven't run the formatter, the TypeScript check or the app, because those commands needed approval I didn't have. Please run `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend format` and `typescript:check`, then try it in a notebook with a table.

**Changes from your draft:**

- **Typed commands:** `runCommand` now takes a list of the allowed command names (`addRowBefore`, `deleteColumn`, etc.) instead of `(chain as any)[command]()`. It builds one chain that focuses, moves the cursor into the hovered cell, then runs the command. Before, it made three separate calls.
- **No flash on first show:** the grip position is now worked out during render and applied with `style`. The draft set it in a `useEffect` with no dependencies, which runs after the first paint, so the grip would briefly draw in the wrong place.
- **Fewer re-renders:** the draft saved a new hovered-cell object on every `mousemove`, re-rendering constantly. Now it only updates when the mouse moves to a different cell.
- **Scrolling:** the grips use `position: fixed`, so after a scroll they'd no longer line up with the table. Any scroll now clears the hovered cell and closes an open menu.
- **Finding the table in the document:** the draft computed the table's position with `posAtDOM(table, 0) - 1`. That relies on how Tiptap's table view builds its DOM (wrapper div, `colgroup`). It now takes the cell's position and walks up the document tree to the table node, and gives up safely if the cell has been removed from the page.
- **Selection highlight:** clicking a grip now highlights the row or column in every case, including tables with one row or one column. The draft's two-cell minimum skipped those.
- **Smaller fixes:** I used `IconArrowUp` and `IconArrowDown` instead of a rotated `IconArrowRight`, built class names with `clsx`, and added `aria-label`s to the grip buttons.

**Decision for you:** the old menu had a "Delete entire table" button, and neither your draft nor this version has one. Tell me if you want it back, for example as the last item in both menus.
